Introduction to Stata

Why Stata?





Stata (/’steIt@/ ) is a general-purpose statistical software package developed by
StataCorp.

   A powerful statistical software that enables users to analyze, manage, and
     produce graphical visualizations of data.

     Despite not being open-source, Stata offers an extensive range of oﬀicial and
     user-written commands.

     Widely used for academic research, especially in the field of economics and
     finance. See paper replication packages at AEA website.

    Other advantages are fast, accurate, and easy to use.

Introduction to Stata

Stata file format





     Stata works with 3 key file formats that are integral to its data management
    and analysis processes
          “.dta” files: store datasets in Stata’s native format
          “.do” files: scripts that contain a series of Stata commands
         “.ado” files: define custom commands or programs to extend Stata’s
           functionality

Introduction to Stata

First steps: create your do-file


     Write all your codes in the do-file editor. Do not click the manual or write
     your command in the interface frequently
     Press ”Ctrl+D” to run the selected command





            TA Group                                CUHK(SZ)                               September 9, 2024          11 / 22

Introduction to Stata

First steps: working directory





    To see your working directory, type:

                             pwd

    To change the working directory to avoid typing the whole path when calling
     or saving files, type:

                             cd “c:\my path”





            TA Group                                CUHK(SZ)                               September 9, 2024          12 / 22

Introduction to Stata

First steps: log file




Create a log file, sort of Stata’s built-in tape recorder and where you can:
1) retrieve the output of your work and 2) keep a record of your work.

    To create a log file, type:

                                log using mylog.log

     This will create the file ’mylog.log’ in your working directory. You can read it
     using any word processor (notepad, word, etc.).

    To close a log file, type:

                                      log close

Introduction to Stata

Opening/saving Stata files (*.dta)



To open files already in Stata with the extension *.dta, run Stata and you can
either:
    Go to file→open in the menu, or
    Type

                       use “c:\mydata\mydatafile.dta”

       If your working directory is already set to c:\mydata, just type

                             use “mydatafile”,clear

    To save a data file from Stata go to file –save as or just type:

                           save “my datafile”,replace

Introduction to Stata

Variable type

Stata has a color-coded system for each type. Black is for numbers, red is for text
or string and blue is for labeled variables
     For numeric variables, you can do any statistical procedure with this variable
     For string variables, even though you see numbers, you can’t do any
      statistical procedure with this variable other than simple frequencies
     For labeled variables, you can do any statistical procedure

Introduction to Stata

Frequently used commands





     tostring, destring: change numerical (string) variable to string (numerical)
     variable

     describe: describe variable names, storage type, display format, label

    summarize: mean, std, min, max

     tabulate: frequency of value

    rename: rename variable

     generate: generate new variable

    keep, drop: keep or drop variables

    Help file is always your best teacher!!! just type ”help + command”, for
    example

                                   help regress
